title: A module sheaf pulled back from an algebraically closed point is constant
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $K$ an algebraically closed field, $Y$ a scheme and $e:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme]. For every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], there is a $\Lambda$-module $M$ and an isomorphism $e^{-1}F\cong\underline M$ on $Y$, with inverse image as in [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and constant sheaf as in [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. No torsion, finiteness, or nonvanishing hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Apply the set-valued geometric-point constancy theorem to the module sheaf after forgetting to sets. Its constant-sheaf counit is invertible.

The Mathlib constantSheafAdj_counit_w comparison identifies the image of the module-valued counit with the composite of the constant-sheaf comparison isomorphism and the set-valued counit. Forgetting modules reflects isomorphisms, so the module counit is invertible. Its source is constant with value the global sections module M.
Pull back the inverse of the module counit, then compose with upperStarConstantSheafIso applied to M.

theorem exists_constant_module_upperStar_geometricPoint
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] {K : Type u} [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K]
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (e : Y ⟶ Spec (.of K))
    (F : Sheaf (Spec (.of K)).smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) :
    ∃ M : ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ,
      Nonempty ((upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) e).obj F ≅
        (constantSheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).obj M)
